messages:
anya: Quick sync — proposing an incremental attribute canonicalization for console telemetry (route attributes currently live as freeform jsonb). plan: add canonical_attr column, dual-write from API, backfill in background, then switch reads with COALESCE. low-risk, supports smaller dashboard queries. :rocket:

mike: sketch the schema change? any index fallout?

anya: SQL we discussed:
```sql
ALTER TABLE console_events ADD COLUMN canonical_attr TEXT;
-- populate with normalized value where possible
UPDATE console_events SET canonical_attr = (payload->>'route_attr') WHERE canonical_attr IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_console_events_canonical_attr ON console_events USING btree (canonical_attr);
```
No locking expected except the update which we will chunk.

jeremy: chunking plan? we should avoid long txns on the hot partition.

anya: plan is 1) dual-write at API level behind ff `route_attr_v2` 2) background backfill job that processes 5k rows/sec per worker with rate limiter, heartbeat + resume token, chunk size 10k, use COPY to temp table for big updates. will monitor lag.

mike: how do reads change while backfill is running? dashboards need stable queries.

tess: yes, Console dashboards rely on route attr for group_by. if some rows still only have jsonb, queries must behave identical.

anya: read fallback: use COALESCE(canonical_attr, (payload->>'route_attr')) in materialized views and API layer. example in SQL views:
```sql
SELECT COALESCE(canonical_attr, payload->>'route_attr') AS route_attr_norm, count(*)
FROM console_events
GROUP BY route_attr_norm;
```
That keeps results consistent during rollout.

sam: what about quota evaluation paths? those touch heavy ingest. dual-write overhead ok?

jeremy: dual-write must be idempotent and non-blocking. do it async for ingest hot path: write to primary, then enqueue dualwrite job to write canonical_attr to analytics table. schema change on downstream stores will be eventual consistent. for Dedicated we can enable sync path behind enterprise flag if needed.

mike: retention/backfill safety: how long do we keep dual-write code and legacy column?

anya: propose 8 weeks: 2w canary, 4w full backfill, 2w grace. After that drop jsonb accessor dependencies and the legacy column removal run. removal will be a separate, announced migration with dry-run mode.

tess: UX note — when we flip the default read to canonical_attr we should add a console rollout toggle that flips per-org query path so support can debug mismatches. also add a rollout dashboard: mismatch rate, backfill progress, query latency delta.

anya: good call. we'll add metrics: `route_attr_mismatch_rate`, `backfill_rows_processed`, `dualwrite_error_rate`, `view_query_latency_p50` and p95.

jeremy: indexing: create index concurrently after backfill or before?

anya: create index concurrently early (non-blocking) but avoid relying on it until backfill completes. for hot partitions we may do partial indexes for common prefixes first.

sam: any migration hooks for private deployments? on-prem customers may want offline scripts.

anya: we'll produce an ops playbook and an `offline-backfill.sh` that supports batch COPY + update. include checksums and sample queries to verify parity.

mike: fallback queries with COALESCE are fine but we should patch the ORM read layer so engineers don't forget to use COALESCE in ad-hoc queries. maybe add a lint rule or DB view abstraction.

anya: agreed — we'll ship a DB view `console_events_v2` that exposes `route_attr_norm` and force teams to use that as canonical source. doc and lint + console deprecation note.

infra-bot: deploy: migration job queued to run on staging at 03:00 UTC tomorrow.

tess: will run dashboard smoke on staging after migration. I'll grab a canary org to validate group_by parity. :eyes:

anya: thanks all — I'll write the runbook and PR with feature-flag gating. posting the checklist here once ready.
